note: Hand-fixed from a real run's crossrepo-links.json, then verified against both source files. Chosen for diversity of the mechanisms that can break independently: literal vs parameterised paths, gin vs express backends, four different backend modules, the literal-over-parameter precedence case, and the two frontend files whose base binding traps (renamed destructure, derived base) would silently point a call at the wrong backend.

links.note: pure literal path; the handler S1's denominator work was built around
parameterised: the frontend template hole must align with the route parameter
same path as leave-read, different method — pins that the method participates in matching
the collection route, distinct from the /me route below
PRECEDENCE: /v2/leaves/me and /v2/leaves/:leave_id both exist; a literal segment must win
express backend: the path exists only after the app.use mount prefix is composed; handler is inline, so none is pinned
a third backend module; also exercises the inline `${config.key}` base form
clientApi.ts renames its base (`clientMainApi: mainApi`); attributing bases by identifier name globally would send this call to the wrong backend

mustUnresolved.note: REAL PRODUCT FINDING: the frontend sends PATCH; the backend registers only GET/PUT on this path. It must stay unresolved — a resolver that 'helpfully' matched it would hide a bug.

floors.note: Gold pins 10 links in 6 frontend files, but the target has 383 links across 32 files. A regression that silently drops a whole client — or a whole backend's route table — can leave every gold pair intact. These floors are what notices that. Re-pinned after 57B-402 made the extractor read call expressions structurally: the previous values (380/480/340) were measured while type-argument calls were silently dropped, so leaving them would have handed the recovered 19 calls straight back. Values are the measured counts with ~7% headroom, so ordinary target churn does not trip them.
